title: Pasta vs. rice: calories, carbs and protein

seo.title: Pasta vs. rice: calories, carbs and protein per 100 g
seo.meta_description: Cooked white pasta has ~158 kcal, 30.9 g carbs and 5.8 g protein/100 g; white rice has ~130 kcal, 28.2 g carbs and 2.7 g protein.
seo.search_intent: Compare cooked pasta and rice for calories, carbohydrates, protein and fiber using equal weights.

excerpt: Compared cooked and per 100 g, white pasta provides a little more energy and carbohydrate than white rice, but more than twice the protein and substantially more fiber: about 158 kcal, 30.9 g carbs, 5.8 g protein and 1.8 g fiber versus 130 kcal, 28.2 g, 2.7 g and 0.4 g.
content_html:
Pasta and rice often fill the same place on a plate, but they are not nutritionally identical gram for gram. The comparison only makes sense in the same food state. Per 100 g cooked, white pasta provides more protein and fiber than white rice, along with somewhat more energy.

Per 100 g cooked

NutrientCooked white pastaCooked white rice
Energy~158 kcal~130 kcal
Carbohydrate~30.9 g~28.2 g
Protein~5.8 g~2.7 g
Fat~0.9 g~0.3 g
Fiber~1.8 g~0.4 g

These are USDA reference values for cooked enriched pasta without added salt and cooked long-grain white rice.

Pasta provides more protein

At about 5.8 g versus 2.7 g per 100 g cooked, pasta provides a little more than twice the protein in this comparison. A 200 g serving would provide roughly 11.6 g from pasta versus 5.4 g from rice.

Rice is somewhat lower in calories per 100 g

The difference is about 28 kcal per 100 g. At 200 g, that is roughly 316 kcal for pasta versus 260 kcal for rice, a gap of about 56 kcal before sauces, oils or toppings.

Water content explains part of the difference

Cooked starches absorb different amounts of water. That is why comparing 100 g dry pasta with 100 g cooked rice would be misleading: the water content is not comparable.

Both are relatively low in fiber when refined

The white pasta entry has about 1.8 g fiber per 100 g, roughly 4.5 times the 0.4 g in white rice. Whole-grain versions of both foods increase fiber substantially.

Which is more filling?

That depends on more than carbohydrate. Portion size, texture, protein, fiber and the rest of the meal all matter. Adding vegetables and a protein source often changes satiety more than switching between plain pasta and rice.

The practical takeaway

Cooked white rice is somewhat lower in calories per 100 g; white pasta provides substantially more protein and fiber. The better choice depends on the whole meal, not a small carbohydrate difference.

faq.question: Which has more calories, pasta or rice?
faq.answer: In cooked references per 100 g, white pasta is about 158 kcal and white rice about 130 kcal.

faq.question: Which has more protein?
faq.answer: Cooked white pasta: about 5.8 g/100 g versus about 2.7 g in cooked white rice.

faq.question: Do they have the same carbohydrates?
faq.answer: They are similar but not identical: about 30.9 g/100 g in cooked pasta and 28.2 g/100 g in cooked white rice.
